scope: One bounded continuation: weighted shared reconstruction and a training-only global count-noise scale, with independent held-out populations and unchanged calibration gates
variance_definition: Pixel-center central second moment minus pixel_width_mm squared / 12; no clipping or distribution-specific fitting
noise_definition: sqrt((fourth_central_moment - (N-3)/(N-1) * second_central_moment squared) / N), computed from each VM particle-count frame
noise_validation: Apply the training-only global noise scale, then compare held-out frame minus calibration mean against sqrt(frame noise variance plus calibration-mean noise variance); no fitting on held-out populations

benchmark.forecast_noise_interpretation: Existing fixed future-query noise assumption retained; only revealed observations receive per-frame noise estimates. No hidden reference or future frame enters pool noise.
benchmark.observations: Actual positive corrected RMS variances from independent elegant particle populations; paired policies reuse the same query-indexed frame, with no additive Gaussian perturbation
benchmark.reference: Frozen primary corrected-image full-scan reference, audited against entrance particle covariance; finite precision, not absolute truth

failure_policy: Retain all invalid frames, nonphysical references, quality failures and unavailable recommendations; no retries, clipping, sample rejection or projection
continuation: Preserve B2/B3/B4. Stop on any unchanged calibration gate failure; run the declared matched-budget comparison only if calibration passes. No further model or acquisition tuning in this stage.
reference_solver: shared weighted SVD with RMS-size errors = per-frame variance std / (2 * sqrt(variance)); no beam-matrix projection
noise_scale_calibration: sqrt(mean over training points of sample variance of corrected measurements divided by mean predicted noise variance)); training only, no point-specific fitted factors
input_frames: Reuse frozen B4 primary and training frames; record source hashes. Independent validation seeds are not reused.
